report.summary: Chunk 5 of markdown.py: fenced code block filtering, link occurrence detection, link resolution, wikilink lookup and hit matching.

handoff.purpose: Provide functions for filtering code blocks, extracting links, resolving document-relative links, and performing wikilink lookup and hit matching.

symbols.name: _content_lines
symbols.note: Generator that yields (line_index, stripped_line) for non-fence lines, used internally.

symbols.name: _link_occurrences
symbols.note: Yields (line_index, DocLink) for every link (inline, reference, autolink, wikilink) in content lines starting from start.

symbols.name: resolve_link
symbols.note: Resolves a document-relative link path to a known file path; returns None if unresolvable.

symbols.name: wiki_lookup
symbols.note: Builds two dictionaries (by full path, by basename) lower-cased with sorted values for deterministic ambiguity checks.

symbols.name: _hits
symbols.note: Returns set of candidate paths matching a wikilink name, handling both vault-root-relative and document-relative interpretations.

claims.text: Standard destinations on a line come first, in their existing order, then the wikilinks on that line.
claims.why: The function yields inline, reference, autolink matches before wikilink matches for each line.

claims.text: The two syntaxes cannot overlap -- ``[[a]]`` contains no ``](`` and ``[a](b)`` contains no ``]]`` -- so nothing is counted twice
claims.why: The claim about non-overlap is based on syntax properties; the code does not verify this, it just iterates separate regex patterns.

claims.text: a document with no ``[[`` yields exactly the sequence this function's predecessor yielded.
claims.why: No previous function is shown; cannot verify equivalence.

claims.text: Returns None when it cannot be resolved -- an unresolved link is DROPPED and counted, never guessed onto a near-match.
claims.why: The function returns None if candidate not in known_files and not found via case-insensitive fallback.

claims.text: ``known_files`` is a set/mapping of rel paths (POSIX, repo-relative).
claims.why: The code uses 'in known_files' and sorted(known_files), which works for sets and mappings, but the type is not enforced.

claims.text: Windows checks out paths case-insensitively, so a doc may spell a link in a case the file set does not use. Mirrors ``graph._resolve_node``'s fallback.
claims.why: The fallback is implemented (lowercased dict), but reference to graph._resolve_node is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Every occurrence lands in exactly one, and the three that produce no edge are COUNTED separately, because they are three different statements: "no such file" (unresolved), "several such files and picking one would be fabrication" (ambiguous), and "this parser does not answer that question in this phase" (deferred).
claims.why: The constants are defined but counting logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Built once per document rather than once per link, and sorted at build time so two processes see candidates in the same order -- an ambiguity verdict that depended on set iteration order would be a coin flip wearing a receipt.
claims.why: The function sorts known_files and builds lists; order is deterministic.

claims.text: A bare note name is Obsidian's "shortest path when possible": it names a file anywhere in the vault. Two files with that basename is exactly the tie this module refuses to break.
claims.why: If '/' not in name, function returns by_base.get(name.lower(), ()) which may have multiple candidates.

claims.text: A path is read BOTH as vault-root-relative (what Obsidian does) and as document-relative (what a reader who knows markdown assumes). When the two readings name two different files that BOTH exist, the link is genuinely ambiguous and gets counted as such -- this is the case B-M2 of the plan names, where the failure mode would otherwise flip from "unresolved" to "silently resolved to the wrong one of two candidates".
claims.why: The function computes both candidates (root-relative and document-relative) and returns the union, potentially including both.

observations.what: _content_lines filters fenced code blocks and removes inline code before yielding lines.
_link_occurrences yields links in a specific order: inline, reference, autolink, then wikilink.
resolve_link uses case-insensitive fallback for known_files, consistent with Windows behavior.
wiki_lookup builds two dictionaries with sorted lists for deterministic iteration.
_hits returns union of root-relative and document-relative candidate sets for paths with '/', potentially causing ambiguity.
